targets.title: Feeling the future: experimental evidence for anomalous retroactive influences on cognition and affect.
targets.evidence_quote: This metascientific project studied the replicability of Bem Experiment 1, which had claimed a precognitive effect, i.e., the ability to successfully guess the outcome of future random events (Bem. J Pers Soc Psychol. 2011;100: 407−25).
targets.outcome_quote: Using this advanced methodology, the present work further disconfirmed the original claim of a precognitive effect in Bem Experiment 1 [ 35 , 36 ].
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit overall disconfirmation of Bem’s original precognitive claim. A below-chance exploratory effect confirmed once and then not confirmed concerns this paper’s own unpublished-internal studies and is not another published target or support for Bem’s above-chance claim.

reasoning: Publisher full article verified by title, DOI, and all seven authors (the XML also names an editor, who is excluded). Bem 2011 Experiment 1 is the specific primary finding re-tested. Bem et al. 2016 is a meta-analysis of the claim, not a second primary original. Kekecs et al. 2023 supplies the consensus TPP methods, software and analysis routines rather than a separately selected finding target. AMP and other psi references provide controls/background. Study 1 directly tests Bem; Studies 2–3 test a new internal below-chance effect, so they do not create another original-paper entry. Overall original-claim verdict is failed. Saved extraction excludes appended peer-review subarticles and retains the article reference list.
